what_happened: Counsel for ADR and other petitioners mentioned seven petitions against the Bihar revision, and the Court let them be filed during the vacation and listed them for 10 July 2025.

source: Supreme Court of India (judgment of 27.05.2026, 2026 INSC 564, para 10.8)
what_happened: The Court issued notice to the Commission and said the petitions raised three questions about its power, its method and the timing before the Bihar election, according to the account in the Court's 2026 judgment.

The Court recorded the Commission's agreement to publish, district by district and searchable by EPIC number, the list of about 65 lakh electors left off the Bihar draft roll with the reason for each.
The Court directed the Commission to accept Aadhaar as proof of identity for the Bihar revision and said it is no proof of citizenship.

issues: Notices and hearings; Transparency of lists
what_happened: The Court recorded that about 1.40 crore people in West Bengal had been sent notices and directed that names in the logical discrepancy list be displayed at panchayat, block and ward offices.

parties_and_bodies: Trinamool Congress; Government of West Bengal; Election Commission; District Election Officer
issues: Notices and hearings; Adjudication and appeals
what_happened: The order records that Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee appeared in her own petition on 4 February 2026, and the Court directed the 8,505 officers the state offered to report to the district officers.

The Court recorded the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court's report that over 10,16,000 objections had been disposed of, and directed that appeals against the judicial officers' orders go to tribunals of former Chief Justices and judges.

issues: Adjudication and appeals; Police and FIRs
what_happened: After seven judicial officers deciding SIR objections were surrounded at a BDO office in Maldah district, the Court directed central forces for them and directed the Commission to give the inquiry to an independent agency such as the CBI or the NIA.
The Court directed that appeals the tribunals decided by 21 or 27 April 2026, before polling, be given effect in a supplementary roll, and said a pending appeal gave no right to vote.
The Supreme Court's judgment of 27 May 2026 records that some petitions, W.P.(C) 855 of 2025 among them, were filed in support of the revision and asked for it to be held at regular intervals.

The Court held the Bihar revision lawful under section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act read with Article 324 and said declining to enrol someone does not declare that person not to be a citizen.

issues: Deletions; Living electors marked dead; Adjudication and appeals
source: Supreme Court of India (2026 INSC 564, para 186(h))
what_happened: The Court directed the Commission to refer within four weeks the cases it deleted as non-citizens to the authority under the Citizenship Act and allowed people in Bihar wrongly deleted as absent, dead, shifted or duplicate to seek judicial review.

source: High Court for the State of Telangana (order reproduced by LiveLaw)
what_happened: A Charminar voter asked the High Court to restore his family's deleted names, and the Court dismissed the petition and told him to use the revision then under way.
Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra asked the Supreme Court to quash the Commission's order of 24 June 2025 and to stop it from ordering the same revision in other states, LiveLaw reported.

issues: Duplicates and errors; Schedule and deadlines
what_happened: A former AIADMK MLA asked the Madras High Court to order a re-verification of 229 booths in T. Nagar, and the Court adjourned the case after the Commission said the revision would begin within a week, LiveLaw reported.

A PIL asked the Calcutta High Court to have the West Bengal revision use the current roll in place of the 2002 roll and to protect booth level officers, and the Court asked the Commission for an affidavit, The Week reported.

parties_and_bodies: DMK; CPI(M); Congress; Trinamool Congress; Election Commission
what_happened: The Court issued notice on the petitions against the second phase in Tamil Nadu and West Bengal and asked the High Courts to hold back their own cases on the revision, The Leaflet reported.

The Kerala government asked the High Court to put off the revision until the local body elections ended, and the Court dismissed the petition because the Supreme Court had asked High Courts to hold back such cases, SCC Online reported.

On a TVK application saying 35 to 40 booth level officers had died under work pressure, the Court suggested that states provide more staff and cut working hours in proportion, National Herald reported.

parties_and_bodies: Government of Kerala; IUML; Congress; CPI(M); Election Commission
what_happened: The Kerala government and leaders of the IUML, Congress and CPI(M) asked for more time for enumeration forms, and the Court put off a decision to 18 December, LiveLaw reported.
A PIL asked the Allahabad High Court to apply the Commission's revision guidelines to Uttar Pradesh's panchayat rolls, and the Court dismissed it, LiveLaw reported.

The Surat district Congress president and a Seva Dal organiser asked the Gujarat High Court to reject objections not filed under the rules, to act against false objections and to halt the revision, LawTrend reported.

Residents displaced by a 2023 demolition said they were left out of the Uttar Pradesh revision, and the Court sent them to the district election officer with liberty to go to the Allahabad High Court, Verdictum reported.

Counsel told the Court that 136 of nearly 27 lakh appeals had been decided, and the Court declined fresh grievances and sent the parties to the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court, Supreme Court Observer reported.

Adivasi Sena asked the Telangana High Court to have non-tribal voters it called ineligible removed from the rolls of the Fifth Schedule Areas during the revision, and the Court sought replies, Telangana Today reported.

Petitioners asked the Telangana High Court to strike the state's Family Register Certificate from the revision's list of documents, and the Court gave the Commission time and listed the case for 12 August, Telangana Today reported.

A PIL asked the Delhi High Court for special arrangements so homeless and displaced people could enrol in the revision, and the Court reserved its order and said it would not monitor the policy, LiveLaw reported.

A man deleted in the revision said it was blocking his passport renewal, and the Calcutta High Court told the appellate tribunal to decide his appeal within two weeks without going into the merits, LiveLaw reported.

Delhi Congress president Devender Yadav challenged the Form 6 declaration that deleted voters must sign as first-time applicants, and he withdrew the petition after the Court told him to file it as a PIL, LiveLaw reported.

issues: Notices and hearings; Transparency of lists
what_happened: Activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri asked for the list of Delhi voters sent notices and the criteria for logical discrepancies, and the bench told the Commission to look at extra safeguards, ThePrint reported.

A family of six told the court that they had moved house within the same constituency and filed Form 8 on a BLO's instruction, and that they were then deleted from the roll because the ERONET software found no record of their cards and allowed only a rejection. The bench asked the Commission to show where the law allows a deletion without a hearing and said the family should not have been asked to file Form 6, The Wire reported, citing The Times of India.
commission_reply: The Wire reported that the Commission's counsel said other voters removed in the same way had been put back on the roll after filing Form 6, and that the family had not filed Form 6 when asked to.

what_happened: A petition asked the Court to quash 14 decisions it said the Chief Election Commissioner took alone, and the Court issued notice, tagged it with a similar case and said it had not approved any modified Form 6, LiveLaw reported.

At a further hearing of the same family's petition the bench asked what purpose the revision served if citizens were left off the roll. It also asked why a voter who had moved house should have to sign the enumeration form, whose declaration says the voter still lives at the address on the existing roll, LiveLaw reported.
commission_reply: LiveLaw reported that the Commission's counsel argued that a voter had to submit the enumeration form along with Form 8 to have an address changed, and that a voter who did not submit it had to file Form 6.

what_happened: The Chief Justice's bench refused an oral request to order that no names be deleted from the roll in Maharashtra for the time being. It said it would follow the Supreme Court, which it was told had restrained High Courts in November 2025 from hearing petitions on the revision, and adjourned the case by four weeks, LiveLaw reported. The petition asks for the order and reasons behind the revision in the state and for safeguards against wrongful exclusion.

The Week, carrying a PTI report, said the Jharkhand Assembly passed a resolution opposing the SIR, moved by Parliamentary Affairs Minister Radhakrishna Kishore on behalf of the INDIA bloc. The BJP opposed it. When a Congress member asked for a vote, the Speaker ruled that it stood passed because the ruling coalition had a majority.

The Siasat Daily, carrying a PTI report, said the Kerala Assembly unanimously passed a resolution moved by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan against the SIR in the state, with the Congress-led opposition backing it.
ETV Bharat reported that a Bihar bandh called by the INDIA bloc parties against the SIR disrupted life across much of the state, with Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav taking part.

Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said opposition members protested against the SIR inside the Bihar Assembly on the first day of its monsoon session, with CPI(ML) Liberation legislators wearing black.
ETV Bharat reported that INDIA bloc MPs protested at the Makar Dwar of Parliament against the Bihar SIR for a fifth day running and demanded that it be rolled back.

issues: Protest and march; Police and FIRs
what_happened: The Wire reported that Delhi Police detained opposition MPs, among them Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, when their march from Parliament to the Election Commission against the Bihar SIR was stopped, and that they were released in the afternoon.
commission_reply: The Wire reported that the Commission had written to Jairam Ramesh the day before asking for the names of 30 members for a meeting “due to limitation of space”.

what_happened: ETV Bharat reported that Rahul Gandhi began a 16-day Vote Adhikar Yatra from Sasaram against the SIR in Bihar, due to end with a rally in Patna on 1 September. The Congress leader alleged that the SIR was being done to steal votes.

The News Minute reported that an all-party meeting chaired by Chief Minister M.K. Stalin, attended by nearly 50 parties, resolved to approach the Supreme Court against the SIR in Tamil Nadu. The AIADMK and the BJP were not invited and several other parties stayed away.
ETV Bharat reported that Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee led a procession in Kolkata against the SIR. She called the SIR an assault on people's existence and democratic rights.
Akashvani News reported that the DMK and its alliance partners held protest demonstrations across Tamil Nadu against the SIR, with MPs, MLAs and district functionaries taking part.
The Tribune reported that Mamata Banerjee led a three-km march from Bongaon to Thakurnagar in North 24 Parganas against the SIR, after addressing a rally at Bangaon.
commission_reply: The Tribune reported that the Commission granted a five-member TMC delegation a meeting on 28 November.

parties_and_bodies: Congress; Election Commission; Government of Assam
what_happened: The Siasat Daily, carrying a PTI report, said the united opposition held a protest at Chachal in Guwahati against alleged irregularities in the draft rolls of Assam's Special Revision. Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi accused Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma of misusing the Election Commission.
commission_reply: The report said the Commission stated that the flagged names had not yet been deleted and would only be processed after formal applications in the claims and objections period.

what_happened: ETV Bharat reported that trade unions, women's groups, student bodies and Dalit and minority rights groups protested against the SIR at Freedom Park in Bengaluru under the banner My Vote, My Right, and urged the state government to take a stand.

issues: Protest and march; Adjudication and appeals
what_happened: ETV Bharat reported that Mamata Banerjee ended her sit-in against the SIR on its fifth day after the Supreme Court ordered appellate tribunals to hear appeals against exclusions in West Bengal. She said the protest was suspended temporarily.

ETV Bharat reported that a Congress delegation led by Kumari Selja staged a sit-in outside the Election Commission headquarters in Delhi over the SIR in Uttarakhand after saying it was not allowed into the premises.

Business Today reported that Congress workers protested in several states demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the handling of the SIR, after The Indian Express reported objections recorded by two Election Commissioners.
commission_reply: Business Today reported that the Commission rejected the characterisation of these exchanges as institutional dissent and said final decisions on the SIR were unanimous.

what_happened: Business Today reported that police detained Assam Congress president and MP Gaurav Gogoi during a protest in Guwahati demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.

parties_and_bodies: Civil society groups; CPI(ML) Liberation; Police
what_happened: The Quint reported that police detained protesters from civil society groups and student organisations at Jantar Mantar, among them CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya, as they demanded the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation and a rollback of the SIR.

ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said police detained Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai and hundreds of party workers in Lucknow after they were stopped while marching to demand the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.

ThePrint, carrying an ANI report, said police used water cannons on Congress workers in Patna who were protesting against the Chief Election Commissioner as part of the party's nationwide programme over the SIR.
commission_reply: The report said the Commission described operational queries and internal feedback as part of the normal functioning of a multi-member body and said all final SIR decisions were unanimous.

what_happened: ThePrint, carrying an ANI report, said police used water cannons on Punjab Congress workers demonstrating in Chandigarh as part of the party's protests over the SIR.

ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said the Himachal Pradesh Congress protested outside the Election Commission office in Shimla, burned an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner and raised slogans against the SIR.

UNI reported that Congress workers in Shillong, led by state Congress president Vincent H. Pala, burned an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner and demanded his removal amid the row over the SIR.

Asianet Newsable reported that the Uttarakhand Congress marched in Dehradun, surrounded the Election Commission office and burned an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner. The party raised concerns over how names were added and deleted and how objections were disposed of.

ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said the Karnataka Congress, with Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, protested at Freedom Park in Bengaluru against the SIR and demanded the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.
commission_reply: The Election Commission, however, has asserted that its official orders, decisions and administrative directions have full legal sanction, and that differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberations within any institution.

what_happened: ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said police used water cannons and detained former Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot and state Congress chief Govind Singh Dotasra during a march to the State Election Commission office in Jaipur over alleged SIR irregularities.

Leaders of the INDIA bloc, 33 of them from 19 parties, agreed a plan of district marches from 2 to 8 October, a march of opposition MPs to the Commission on 6 October, a meeting with the President in the second week of October and five rallies including one in Delhi on 1 November, The Wire reported. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the Commission was being used as a puppet by the Prime Minister and the Home Minister.

The South First reported that more than a dozen civil society groups held a day-long protest at Dharna Chowk in Hyderabad, demanding that the SIR be scrapped and the Chief Election Commissioner resign.

The Free Press Journal reported that Uddhav Thackeray of the Shiv Sena (UBT) and Raj Thackeray of the MNS led the Virat Garjana Morcha in Mumbai seeking the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation. Raj Thackeray demanded that the SIR in Maharashtra be cancelled.

issues: Protest and march; Police and FIRs
what_happened: The Wire reported that police stopped an INDIA bloc march from Parliament to the Election Commission, and that opposition MPs held a sit-in at the All India Radio building until police detained Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra that night.

Opposition MPs of the INDIA bloc marched from Parliament to the Commission's headquarters to press for the Chief Election Commissioner's removal, and asked for 240 MPs to meet the three Commissioners at Parliament House Annexe, Deccan Herald reported.
commission_reply: The Commission said no party had sought an appointment until 4 pm, that a meeting of 240 MPs away from its premises was unusual and could not be accepted, and that the MPs declined its offer to send its senior-most officer on duty to receive their memorandum, Deccan Herald reported.

what_happened: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said AAP workers and members of other parties protested outside the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation over alleged SIR irregularities. It said AAP had earlier protested at Jantar Mantar and India Gate.

parties_and_bodies: INDIA bloc; Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi; Congress; Police
what_happened: The Tribune reported that Delhi leaders of the INDIA bloc marched to the Election Commission office and gave the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer a memorandum demanding that the SIR be cancelled and excluded eligible voters be restored. It said police detained Delhi Congress president Devender Yadav at a separate protest at Jantar Mantar.

parties_and_bodies: Booth level officers; Teachers' unions; Chief Electoral Officer, Kerala
issues: BLO workload; Deaths; Protest and march

commission_reply: The News Minute reported that Kerala's Chief Electoral Officer said he had not received any complaints regarding work pressure from BLOs.

parties_and_bodies: Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu
issues: BLO workload; Schedule and deadlines; Protest and march
what_happened: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said the Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu began a statewide boycott of SIR work over workload, staff shortages, deadline pressure and poor training.

parties_and_bodies: BLO Adhikar Raksha Committee; Police; Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal
what_happened: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said booth level officers marching under the BLO Adhikar Raksha Committee clashed with police outside the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer's office in Kolkata over SIR workload.
commission_reply: Deccan Herald reported that Chief Electoral Officer Manoj Agarwal described the BLOs as the "real heroes" of the exercise.

what_happened: The Wire reported that nearly 250 primary school teachers working as booth level officers stopped work and held a sit-in at a data uploading centre in Ahmedabad, alleging threats and pressure during the SIR.

parties_and_bodies: Uttar Pradeshiya Prathmik Shikshak Sangh; Teachers' unions
what_happened: Amar Ujala reported that teachers' organisations in Uttar Pradesh, among them the Uttar Pradeshiya Prathmik Shikshak Sangh, objected to the deaths of teachers and staff on SIR duty and demanded jobs and compensation for their families.
Deccan Chronicle reported the Commission saying that about 87 per cent of Bihar's 7.96 crore voters had been given semi-filled enumeration forms on the first booth officer visit.

LiveLaw reported that the Association for Democratic Reforms told the Supreme Court that enumeration forms in Bihar were being uploaded by officials without voters' knowledge or consent. This is ADR's allegation in a court filing.
commission_reply: LiveLaw reported that ADR filed the rejoinder in reply to the Commission's counter-affidavit.

issues: Form 7; Pre-printed forms; Police and FIRs
what_happened: National Herald reported that Trinamool workers stopped a vehicle in Khatra, Bankura said to carry thousands of pre-filled Form 7s, that police seized it and began an inquiry, and that both parties traded allegations over bulk Form 7s on the last day for filing.
commission_reply: National Herald reported that the BJP alleged its workers were attacked and prevented from filing forms inside government offices.

what_happened: Scroll reported that Rajasthan Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra alleged that computer-printed Form 7s were distributed in every constituency and that booth agents' signatures were forged, and demanded a forensic inquiry. These are the Congress's allegations.
commission_reply: Scroll reported that BJP minister Gautam Dak said a voter proposed for removal gets time to be heard and that the Congress wanted to create a dispute.

issues: Form 7; Pre-printed forms; Notices and hearings
what_happened: Scroll reported that during Assam's Special Revision a booth officer in Karimganj North was handed objections against 133 voters on forms she described as half printed and half handwritten, and that hearings were suspended in three Nagaon constituencies after complaints of fake Form 7s.
commission_reply: Scroll quoted a senior Commission official in Guwahati saying a voter can file any number of objections but that an ERO reviews them individually when one person files more than five.

what_happened: Scroll reported that at least seven people named as objectors on Form 7s in Assam, some of them BJP booth agents and members, said they had not filed the objections.
commission_reply: Scroll quoted BJP MP Kamakhya Prasad Tasa as saying anyone can file objections and that it is for the Election Commission to take a final call.

what_happened: The Indian Express reported that Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma told reporters he had told BJP members to keep filing complaints against people he called 'Miyas' and to fill Form 7s wherever possible during the Special Revision.

ETV Bharat reported that Bhopal's Collector ordered a probe after a man named as objector on Form 7s in Bhopal South-West denied filing them, and that officials found incorrect or fake objector details in several of the district's 9,037 Form 7s.
commission_reply: ETV Bharat quoted District Election Officer Kaushlendra Vikram Singh saying no one's name would be removed without verification.

what_happened: Frontline reported that Congress general secretary K. C. Venugopal wrote to the Commission on 29 January alleging misuse of Form 7 in several states, and that the Commission said there was no limit on forms per voter but that an ERO must verify when one person files more than five.
commission_reply: Scroll reported on 23 January 2026 that a senior Commission official in Guwahati gave the same rule.

what_happened: Scroll reported, citing PTI, that after Assam's final roll the Chief Minister said several deletions had been made on complaints filed by BJP workers.

Newslaundry reported that the 15,663 Form 7s in Somnath were filed by 269 people, each filing 50 or more, that copies it reviewed had the voter's details printed in English and the objector's details handwritten in Gujarati, and that six of the objectors filed affidavits saying they had not filed them.
commission_reply: Newslaundry reported that the District Election Officer, V. N. Upadhyay, said he had deployed six AEROs to verify the objections and assured that no name would be deleted arbitrarily.

what_happened: The Quint reported that thousands of Form 7s in Alwar were filed in the names of BJP booth agents, several of whom said their signatures were forged, and that no FIR or inquiry had been announced a month later.
commission_reply: The Quint reported that calls to the District Magistrate and Sub-Divisional Magistrate for comment went unanswered.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal; Electoral Registration Officer
what_happened: National Herald reported that the Commission wrote to West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer to send all Form 7 objections to EROs by 16 February and dispose of them by statutory procedure, and that it had taken cognisance of reports of Form 7 records being burnt.

parties_and_bodies: District Election Officer; Booth level officers
what_happened: Siasat reported, citing The Indian Express, that Form 7s against 544 voters of a Shamli village were found with a booth officer, said to have been already printed with the voters' EPIC numbers, and that the District Magistrate said the forms were fake and the probe found nothing.
commission_reply: DM Arvind Kumar Chauhan ordered a probe and later said that the case “didn’t have any substance.” “We got an investigation done and found nothing,” he added.

what_happened: Deccan Herald reported that the Gujarat High Court issued notice to the Commission and the state on two petitions seeking a Special Investigation Team inquiry into Form 7 objections filed during the SIR.
commission_reply: Deccan Herald reported that the matter was posted for further hearing on 7 July.

what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported Hyderabad's District Election Officer R. V. Karnan explaining that booth officers would hand out enumeration forms already printed with each elector's details and photograph, which the elector completes and signs.

parties_and_bodies: BJP; AIMIM; Booth level officers; Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana
what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Telangana BJP alleged to the Chief Electoral Officer that booth officers in Hyderabad were handing enumeration forms in bulk to AIMIM leaders at party camps and letting them upload filled forms. This is the BJP's allegation.

parties_and_bodies: BJP; Booth level officers; Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana
what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported that the BJP alleged that some booth officers in Serilingampally uploaded the blank back of enumeration forms to the Commission's app without the voter's details, and asked the Chief Electoral Officer for a probe. This is the BJP's allegation.

The Hindu reported that the Supreme Court agreed to consider an application by Congress MP Tanuj Punia alleging that Form 7 objections in the Uttar Pradesh SIR were filed with false particulars, forged signatures and in the names of people who later denied filing them. The application cited one person filing objections against 32 electors in Hata, Kushinagar, and a UP Congress claim of 700 to 800 objections in four Khalilabad booths.

The Pioneer reported that an Uttarakhand Congress delegation told the Chief Electoral Officer that one person had filed objections against about 6,400 voters and about 1,200 people had filed more than ten each. These are the Congress's figures.
commission_reply: The Pioneer reported that CEO V. V. R. C. Purushottam said the revision followed the rules and that observers had been sent to districts with many objections, and that Additional CEO Vijay Kumar Jogdande said an ERO must scrutinise cases where one person seeks to remove more than five names.

parties_and_bodies: BJP; Electoral Registration Officer; Election Commission
what_happened: Newslaundry reported that 35 people named as objectors on 1,657 Form 7s in Jhabrera, 31 of them BJP booth agents, said in affidavits that their names, EPIC numbers and signatures had been misused.
commission_reply: Newslaundry quoted the Jhabrera ERO saying the objections were cancelled after those named sought to withdraw them and the voters would not be deleted, and that the Election Commission would not order any investigation and those whose names were misused should file an FIR.

what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported, in a story datelined Hyderabad that does not say whether the figure covers the state or the district, that the Commission had received close to 50,000 Form 7 applications against entries in the draft roll, and that parties at a meeting chaired by Hyderabad's District Election Officer asked for the Form 10 lists by Assembly constituency.
commission_reply: Deccan Chronicle reported that officials gave parties the total number of applications at a meeting at the GHMC office but did not share figures by Assembly constituency.

what_happened: Newslaundry reported from its investigation in Uttarakhand that numerous applications were filed to remove Muslim voters from the rolls, many in the names of people it said were associated with the BJP. It reported that some people named as objectors later filed affidavits saying they had never filed the objections and that their names, EPIC numbers and signatures had been used fraudulently.

places: Karol Bagh; Patel Nagar; Sangam Vihar
what_happened: The Hindu reported that Form 10 lists published for 21 to 27 September showed four people in Delhi filing more than ten applications a day through the Commission's ECINET portal, which does not enforce the limit of ten a day for booth agents.

parties_and_bodies: Congress; BJP; Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana

parties_and_bodies: Congress; BJP; Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana

commission_reply: The South First reported that the Chief Electoral Officer, C. Sudharshan Reddy, said at a press briefing that officials would thoroughly verify all Form 7 applications before making any decision.

what_happened: The News Minute reported that AIMIM president Asaduddin Owaisi alleged that Form 7s were being filed to remove Muslim voters and warned of protests, and that Congress leaders said the pre-printed forms found in Goshamahal and Bahadurpura were unsigned and were not accepted by booth officers.

parties_and_bodies: BJP; Police; Government of Karnataka; Chief Electoral Officer, Karnataka
what_happened: The News Minute reported that Karnataka BJP leaders asked the state police chief to review the FIRs against party workers, saying filing several Form 7s is not by itself a crime and the rules set no limit on their number.
commission_reply: The News Minute reported that Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara said ministers had gone to the CEO's office to submit a memorandum.

parties_and_bodies: District Election Officer; BJP; Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana
what_happened: Siasat reported, citing PTI, that Hyderabad's District Election Officer R. V. Karnan said the Form 7s in Goshamahal and Musheerabad were not received in bulk and were rejected, the Goshamahal forms because they were unsigned and the Musheerabad ones because the electors were found living at the address.
commission_reply: Siasat reported that BJP state president N. Ramchander Rao said no BJP booth agents had submitted any such Form 7 applications, and that the Chief Electoral Officer had said bulk forms from a party had to be properly enquired into and verified.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Telangana; District Election Officer; Electoral Registration Officer
what_happened: The News Minute quoted a memo of 5 October in which the Chief Electoral Officer, C. Sudharshan Reddy, told District Election Officers that bulk Form 7 applications had been filed and that EROs should act under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act against anyone who knowingly made a false declaration.
commission_reply: Siasat reported that the CEO said this action would follow an inquiry. The memo itself was not found on the CEO Telangana website.

issues: Form 7; Pre-printed forms; Police and FIRs
what_happened: The South First reported that the Telangana Congress asked the Hyderabad Police Commissioner to register an FIR and set up a Special Investigation Team over pre-filled Form 7s in three constituencies, and to examine the BJP's role. These are the Congress's allegations.
commission_reply: The South First reported that the Congress said the Police Commissioner had assured it he would study the matter and take action.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Karnataka; Electoral Registration Officer
what_happened: Karnataka's Chief Electoral Officer said 91,278 Form 7 applications were received between 16 June and 4 October, that no name had yet been deleted because of one, and that each would go through a notice and hearing before an officer decided. He said EROs would inquire into bulk applications and that his office had registered no FIR, The News Minute reported.

Deccan Chronicle reported that Asaduddin Owaisi alleged that pre-printed Form 7s seeking the deletion of 122 electors, all Muslim, were submitted at booth 28 in Goshamahal in the name of a BJP supporter, and that the booth officer refused them. This is AIMIM's allegation.
commission_reply: Siasat reported on 5 October, citing PTI, that BJP state president N. Ramchander Rao said no BJP booth agents had submitted any such Form 7 applications.

issues: Form 7; Pre-printed forms; Police and FIRs
what_happened: Telangana Today reported that Chikkadpally police were checking the forms, signatures and voter details in the Musheerabad case and whether similar forms were filed elsewhere, and that the forms had reportedly been rejected.

A Judicial Magistrate First Class in Haldwani ordered the Banbhoolpura police on 6 October to register an FIR and investigate. A booth agent of a party had said that Form 7s seeking to delete 28 voters in part 134 were filed online in his name without his knowledge, and the court held that tracing who filed them needed a police investigation, Haldwani Express News reported.
commission_reply: Haldwani Express News reported that the police had told the court the complaint concerned SIR Form 7s and that the complainant could object before the assistant returning officer.

parties_and_bodies: Electoral Registration Officer; Police; BJP; Congress
issues: Form 7; Pre-printed forms; Police and FIRs
what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Musheerabad ERO filed a police complaint, and Chikkadpally police registered a case, against a BJP booth agent who tried to submit 30 pre-printed Form 7s, the first such case in Telangana.
commission_reply: Deccan Chronicle reported that the Congress welcomed the case and asked the police to find who printed and supplied the forms.

what_happened: The Commission announced in May 2025 that it was building ECINET, one platform to bring together more than 40 of its apps and websites for voters, election officials and other users.
The Supreme Court recorded, from the documents before it, what the logical discrepancy category in West Bengal covered and that about 1.36 crore voters fell in it.
The Commission launched ECINET formally on 22 January 2026 and said its trial version had already been used during the Bihar election and the SIR.
Meghalaya's Chief Electoral Officer listed six checks that ECINET used to flag mapping discrepancies in the third phase, among them a sibling age gap under nine months.

After its full meeting on 26 September 2026 the Commission said field officers have access to ECINET by role, set up a committee with an independent expert to check ECINET against the law, and said new IT modules would first go to a committee of officers.
Booth officers in Bhopal told the Free Press Journal they were asked to upload 100 forms a day and could not, because the booth officers' app server was down or very slow.

issues: Notices and hearings; Software (ECINET/ERONET); Transparency of lists
what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported, from internal Commission records it acquired, that the Commission's software initially flagged 1.31 crore voters in West Bengal and 2.35 crore in Madhya Pradesh for logical discrepancies, and that officials had no written instructions on how to resolve them. It reported that no criteria for deciding which flagged voters to summon had been made public.
commission_reply: The Collective said the Commission did not answer its question on how flagged voters were chosen, and that questions sent to the Commission and three state offices on testing and procedure went unanswered.

what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported that on 29 December 2025 the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer's office told state officials in writing that the logical discrepancy software was faulty because the 2002 roll had not been digitised accurately.
commission_reply: The Collective said the Commission and the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer did not reply to its questions on the WhatsApp instructions.

issues: Notices and hearings; Duplicates and errors
source: Siasat (IANS, citing officials of the Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal)
what_happened: Officials of West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer told IANS that the logical discrepancy check caught people who had falsely linked themselves to unrelated voters, and gave examples they said were found at hearings.

The New Indian Express reported that the Android version of the booth officers' app was updated 31 times between 13 November 2025 and 20 January 2026, with no user manual for the updates, and that officials relied on the app to learn what the revision allowed.
The same report quoted a Chennai booth officer who said the app often froze on her phone, so that data was lost or finished work had to be done again.

The Reporters' Collective reported that hearing notices in West Bengal were generated in bulk by the Commission's software for logical discrepancies, and that two EROs it spoke to, with a few deputies, were signing 4,000 to 5,000 printed notices each day. It reported that the software transliterated names from Bengali into English before matching, so that spellings such as Xalxo and Khalkho triggered a discrepancy. The Collective said this showed the Commission had misled the Supreme Court, where it said there was no automated generation of notices.
commission_reply: The Collective said the Commission had not responded by publication. It set its finding against the Commission's submission to the Court that "There is no automated generation of notices" and that officers were "signing them off after application of mind".

what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported that in West Bengal the logical discrepancy check flagged five kinds of mismatch, from spelling differences between the Bengali 2002 roll and the English draft to age gaps with parents and grandparents.
commission_reply: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and had no answer by publication.

parties_and_bodies: Electoral Registration Officer; District Election Officer
what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported that a registration officer showed its reporter that the button to clear voters with a name mismatch had disappeared from ERONET since that morning, so such cases now needed the district officer's approval.
commission_reply: The Collective said it sent detailed questions to the Commission and had no answer by publication.

what_happened: The Indian Express reported that the online Form 6 on the Commission's ECINET portal carried a new declaration asking whether the applicant or their parents or grandparents were in the electoral roll of the last SIR, although the statutory form had not been amended. It reported that the section was not marked mandatory but applicants could not proceed to submission without completing it, and that the downloadable Form 6 on the same portal did not include it.
commission_reply: The EC did not respond to a request for comment and Legislative Department Secretary Rajiv Mani could not be reached despite repeated attempts.

what_happened: The Hindu reported that 13 days into the Karnataka SIR only 0.41% of enumeration forms had been submitted online, and that voters complained of captcha failures, server errors and an ECINet search that failed to find records appearing in the published rolls. It reported that online submission required a current mobile number linked to the voter's EPIC.
commission_reply: Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer V. Anbu Kumar said the process was still under way. However, the CEO did not comment on the technical glitches reported by voters.

what_happened: Deccan Chronicle reported that people filling in enumeration forms on ECINET in Telangana kept being sent back to the home page, and an official put it down to the load from voters in more than a dozen states at once.

issues: Form 6; Commission's independence; Documents and declaration
what_happened: The Indian Express reported, from internal records it investigated, that on May 16 Election Commissioner Vivek Joshi recorded that Form 6 is prescribed by statute and cannot be altered without amending the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and that Commissioner Sukhbir Singh Sandhu concurred on May 19. It reported that the declaration was added to the online form anyway, and that on August 13 Sandhu wrote that the changes were unauthorised and illegal and must be removed immediately.

The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi warned on file, from November 2025 to August 2026, that control of the electoral roll software was being centralised in the Commission's IT division. It reported that on August 14 Sandhu wrote that many Chief Electoral Officers, District Election Officers and Electoral Registration Officers had told him they lacked proper and complete access to ERONet, and that on July 29 both Commissioners wrote separately to the Cabinet Secretary about a change in work allocation.
commission_reply: The Election Commission and the two ECs, Sandhu and Joshi, did not respond to calls and questionnaires emailed by The Indian Express seeking comment.

what_happened: The Hindu reported that up to 11 categories of logical discrepancy were being applied in the third phase of the SIR, up from four when the concept was introduced in West Bengal. They include a sibling age gap of nine months or less, which flagged a Delhi resident's twin children, and a marital mapping mismatch where a woman is linked to her father in the old roll and her husband in the new. It reported that the term has never been clearly defined in any official communication.

parties_and_bodies: Electoral Registration Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, Goa; Election Commission
what_happened: The Indian Express reported that Goa's Electoral Registration Officers heard electors flagged for logical discrepancies and found 97 of them eligible, but could not reverse the earlier decisions on ECINET because the permission was controlled from Delhi. It reported that the Goa Chief Electoral Officer's office wrote eight times in seven days asking for a rollback option, and that all 97 were missing from the final roll published on February 21 and were still missing on September 20.
commission_reply: Goa's Chief Electoral Officer, Sanjay Goel, told the paper the decision not to include them was the Commission's. The Indian Express later reported that the Commission said, after its meeting of 26 September, that 81 of the 97 had filled Form 6 and that the Chief Electoral Officer had been told to help include them.

what_happened: Commission officials said ECINET is decentralised, that each field officer acts through their own login, and that nobody at headquarters can perform those officers' statutory functions. ERONET is now part of ECINET.

parties_and_bodies: Electoral Registration Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi
what_happened: The Hindu reported that more than 350 Delhi electors had been marked ineligible within a month of hearings, about 200 of them in Vikaspuri, and officials said the marking could not be rolled back by the registration officer or the state's Chief Electoral Officer.
commission_reply: The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer wrote to officers on 25 September 2026 setting a 10-point checklist before marking anyone ineligible and telling them not to delete names on flimsy or frivolous grounds.

parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, Maharashtra; Election Commission
what_happened: Outlook, citing NDTV, reported that Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer S Chockalingam asked for four changes to the ECINET software and more discretion for registration officers in logical discrepancy cases.
commission_reply: The Commission said on 26 September that several portal upgrades had already been made on inputs from state Chief Electoral Officers and that further flexibility needed by field officers would be made operational.

what_happened: The Indian Express reported that on the night of 29 to 30 September 2026 the Commission removed the SIR declaration from the online Form 6 on ECINET for states where the final SIR rolls have been published. It reported that the declaration remained for states where the SIR is still ongoing.
commission_reply: The article cites the Commission's September 26 announcement that ‘for non-SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used’.

what_happened: Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh alleged that by restricting registration officers' access to the ECINet roll system and overruling them in Goa, West Bengal and other states, the Commission broke the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
commission_reply: PTI recalled that the Commission, under fire over objections from two of its Commissioners, had said differing views are a normal part of deliberation and that all its orders carry full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.

what_happened: The Indian Express reported a letter of 29 September from the Commission’s Secretary ordering a special drive to enrol "left out and young/first time eligible electors" in the 20 states and union territories where the revision is complete, using the statutory Form 6, with the added declaration kept for the revision phase only. It reported that at a video conference with all Chief Electoral Officers, the states were told to compare the roll from before the revision with the one after, list those removed, visit them at home and help those left out fill in Form 6, with help from the parties’ booth agents.
commission_reply: The letter of 29 September itself was not found. The Commission's letter of 1 October, which continues it, is in the timeline above. The Commission’s press note of 26 September, in the timeline above, had already ordered the drive, and Uttarakhand’s Chief Electoral Officer set out its steps in a press note of 3 October.

parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Electoral Registration Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi
what_happened: The Hindu reported that the options reached Delhi officers on 30 September and only the ten states and union territories where the third phase was still under way, and that a case marked ineligible still could not be reversed.
commission_reply: The Delhi CEO’s office and the EC did not respond to queries on why the options were introduced at this stage.

issues: Form 6; Documents and declaration; Commission's independence
what_happened: Rahul Gandhi of the Congress, the Leader of the Opposition, said the Chief Election Commissioner had changed Form 6 illegally and unilaterally. The Commission replied on X that the statement was misleading, that its Bihar order of 24 June 2025 had the Commission's unanimous approval and was upheld by the Supreme Court on 27 May 2026, and that its press note of 26 September said the declaration attached to Form 6 had been upheld, Business Today reported.

The Indian Express reported that at a meeting on 11 August 2026 more than a dozen West Bengal appeal tribunal judges recorded that the Commission's portal did not let them serve notices, hold virtual hearings, restore a deleted voter or give appellants a copy of the order.
commission_reply: The paper said it emailed the Commission and the Registrar General of the Calcutta High Court on 1 October and received no response.

what_happened: Hindustan Times reported that a security researcher emailed CERT-In on 8 July 2026, copied to the Commission's complaints address, about flaws in the voter-services website and the ECINET app. The worst, in the researcher's account, let anyone obtain election officials' names and mobile numbers without logging in.
commission_reply: HT said neither CERT-In nor the Commission answered its questions of 5 October. On 6 October CERT-In told the researcher that one flaw, the hardcoded encryption key he rated least serious, had been fixed and that work on the rest was under progress. HT said none of the flaws related directly to registration officers' access to the roll, and that the email alleged no theft or misuse of data.

what_happened: Congress alleged after the Hindustan Times report that ECINET was designed to centralise deletions and additions from the BJP's headquarters. This is a party's allegation. Hindustan Times had said none of the flaws it reported related directly to registration officers' access to the roll.
commission_reply: Scroll did not report a response from the Commission to this allegation.

section: Instructions given without a written order
parties_and_bodies: Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal; Trinamool Congress; District Election Officer
what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported that West Bengal's Chief Electoral Officer sent instructions on a WhatsApp group of district magistrates that brought forward the enumeration deadline and asked officers to mark voters absent before the written deadline. The Trinamool Congress had first made the allegation before the Supreme Court.
commission_reply: The Collective said the Commission and the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer did not reply to its questions on the WhatsApp instructions.

section: Instructions given without a written order
parties_and_bodies: District Election Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, West Bengal
issues: Notices and hearings; Documents and declaration; Software (ECINET/ERONET)
what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported that district magistrates of at least three West Bengal districts wrote to the state election office asking for a written procedure for logical discrepancy cases, and that the portal accepted only the 12 listed documents.
commission_reply: The Collective reported that the officers received no response and carried on with their own methods.

section: Instructions given without a written order
what_happened: A registration officer told The Reporters' Collective that officers were told orally to ask unmapped electors for a second document besides Aadhaar, and that the software for a time would not accept Aadhaar alone. The Collective said it could not check this claim.

section: Instructions given without a written order
what_happened: PTI reported that the Commission's written instructions of 14 May 2026 for the third phase told registration officers to refer suspected foreign nationals to the authority under the Citizenship Act.

section: Instructions given without a written order
parties_and_bodies: Electoral Registration Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, Delhi; Election Commission
what_happened: A Delhi registration officer told The Hindu that officers were first told to identify suspected foreigners during enumeration and later told in the middle of it to stop, and that many oral instructions had been taken back.
commission_reply: The Delhi CEO's office and the EC did not respond to The Hindu's queries on why the new ERONET options were introduced at that stage.

section: Instructions given without a written order
what_happened: The Hindu reported that new ERONET options letting registration officers clear notice cases without a hearing or documents were explained only through an eight-minute video from the Commission's IT department, with no written instruction.
commission_reply: The Delhi CEO’s office and the EC did not respond to queries on why the options were introduced at this stage.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
issues: Duplicates and errors; Living electors marked dead
what_happened: The BBC reported that voters in villages near Patna told it the Bihar draft roll carried wrong photographs, duplicate entries and the name of a person who died more than five years earlier. It reported that in Danara village many residents were not sure officials had visited their homes.
commission_reply: In response to the BBC's questions, the Election Commission shared its 24 June order on conducting the SIR and a 27 July press note outlining efforts to ensure no eligible voter was "left behind". "Further, [the commission] does not take any responsibility of any other misinformation or unsubstantiated allegations being floated around by some vested interests," it added. The BBC also noted the commission has said BLOs worked "very responsibly".

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
what_happened: The Wire reported that Mintu Paswan of Ara, Bhojpur, who had been declared dead in the Bihar draft roll, appeared alive in the Supreme Court on 12 August 2025, produced by petitioner Yogendra Yadav. Paswan told The Wire he had filled the enumeration form and that the BLO came to his house only after he complained.
commission_reply: Senior advocate Rakesh Dwivedi, for the Commission, called the production of Paswan "drama". The bench of Justices Surya Kant and Joymalya Bagchi said there may have been an "inadvertent error", which could be rectified.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
parties_and_bodies: Electoral Registration Officer; Booth level officers; Election Commission; Chief Electoral Officer, Bihar
what_happened: Scroll reported that its analysis found 200 booths across 58 constituencies in 26 Bihar districts where between 324 and 641 names were deleted from the draft roll, 77,454 in all. It reported that most deleted voters its team met in 10 of those booths had been marked absent or shifted though they had lived at their addresses for years, and that interviews with 17 BLOs showed no consistent procedure for deciding deletions.
commission_reply: Parth Gupta, electoral registration officer for Purnia, acknowledged that Jhurana Das should not have been asked for her parents' documents, and said, “Please provide her details and I will look into it.” Scroll also reported that Election Commission spokespersons and Bihar Chief Electoral Officer Vinod Singh Gunjiyal did not respond to requests for comment.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
parties_and_bodies: Election Commission; Electoral Registration Officer; Chief Electoral Officer, Bihar
what_happened: The Reporters' Collective reported that a top Commission official and four Bihar EROs confirmed to it that the Commission did not run its de-duplication software during the Bihar SIR and did not give state officials access to it. It quoted the official saying the focus was on document collection. It reported that its own earlier analysis of the final roll found 14.35 lakh suspect duplicate entries.
commission_reply: The Collective said the Commission and Bihar's Chief Electoral Officer did not answer its emailed questions. In person, the Chief Electoral Officer told its reporter "We cannot share this information with you" and said the Supreme Court was hearing the matter.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
what_happened: Newslaundry reported that several voters in Delhi's Okhla constituency whose names were removed before the SIR began said they got no notice or hearing and learnt of the deletion only when they tried to take part in the SIR. It reported that 34,644 names were deleted in Okhla during the 2026 mapping phase, against 9,170 in all of 2025.
commission_reply: Delhi Chief Electoral Officer Ashok Kumar said that no voter had been deleted without an inquiry and an opportunity for a hearing.

section: Wrong entries reported on the rolls
what_happened: Goa's Chief Electoral Officer said on X that 88 of the 97 voters missing from the final roll of February 2026 had filed Form 6 and been accepted, The Pioneer reported. The cases came to light after The Indian Express reported that the Commission's software did not let verified electors be added.

parties_and_bodies: Booth level officers; Police; Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu
what_happened: The Indian Express reported the deaths of two BLOs. The family of Aneesh George in Kannur, Kerala, alleged he was under pressure to finish by December 4, and police said a note found on Mukesh Jangid in Jaipur said he faced extreme pressure from his supervisor and was told he would be suspended if he did not meet his SIR target. It also reported that revenue employees in Tamil Nadu announced a statewide boycott of SIR work over workload.
commission_reply: Kannur District Collector Arun K Vijayan's report indicated that the BLO was not under any work pressure. The Indian Express said its multiple calls and messages to Rajasthan CEO Naveen got no response.

parties_and_bodies: Booth level officers; District Election Officer
what_happened: The Indian Express reported that two women assistant BLOs died of heart attacks in Tapi and Vadodara districts, bringing BLO deaths in Gujarat that week to four. The husband of one, Usha Solanki, said she was a heart patient who had asked to be excused from BLO duty, which the Vadodara Collector disputed.
commission_reply: Vadodara District Collector Anil Dhameliya said, “We checked with the institute as well as with the local officials. She had not made any official request to be excused (from BLO duty)… We have learnt now that she was suffering from a heart ailment and had episodes of fainting in her institute as well.” He also said, “We have been cautious about ensuring that there is no excessive workload on the BLOs and therefore, we have appointed additional staff to assist in the process.” An unnamed government official said, “With a large workforce of over two lakh involved in the SIR work, these deaths can be termed as natural. Linking these to SIR is not justified and logical.”

what_happened: The BBC reported that 10 BLOs it spoke to in Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal said they worked 14 to 15 hours a day with little rest, and that families linked the deaths of more than a dozen poll workers, by alleged suicide or heart attack, to election work stress. The BBC said it had not independently verified the causes of death. It reported BLOs saying the SIR app crashed often and that many had not been paid.
commission_reply: The BBC said the Commission did not answer its questions. It cited media reports of a court affidavit in which the Commission called claims linking booth officers' deaths to the revision "false, exaggerated and politically motivated".

what_happened: The Indian Express reported that Kanchan Kumar Mondal, 75, died of cardiac arrest, according to hospital sources, after falling ill in a queue for an SIR hearing at the Rampurhat-1 block office in Birbhum. His wife and family alleged the SIR process had caused him excessive stress and held the Election Commission responsible. It also reported that Madan Ghosh died of cardiac arrest at an SIR hearing in Howrah the previous day.

issues: Deaths; Notices and hearings; Police and FIRs
what_happened: The New Indian Express, citing PTI, reported that police in Purulia registered an FIR on a complaint by the son of Durjan Majhi, 82, who died allegedly by suicide on 29 December hours before he was due at an SIR hearing. An officer was quoted as saying the case included charges of abetment of suicide and criminal conspiracy against Election Commission officials, with no official named. The family alleged he acted out of anxiety over the SIR.
